The instant Criminal Petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C)/under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS') has been filed by the Petitioner/accused, relating to S.T.C.No.69 of 2024 on the file of the learned II Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, at Eluru, for the offences punishable under Sections 138 and 142 of N.I.Act and 420 of I.P.C.
2.

entities.text: II Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, at Eluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Sri Katam JRNMA Sudheer, learned Counsel for the Petitioner/Accused and Mrs.K.Priyanka Lakshmi, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor on behalf of the State.

3. Learned counsel for the Petitioner would submit that the petition may be disposed of without causing any prejudice to the rights and contentions of the petitioners by dispensing the presence of the Petitioners before the Trial Court.
4. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that the Court may pass appropriate orders.
5. Considering the submissions, the Criminal Petition is disposed of without causing any prejudice to the rights and contentions of the Petitioner.
However, the presence of the Petitioner, before the Trial Court is dispensed with, unless their presence is specifically directed by the Trial Court.

As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
_________________________________________ Dr. JUSTICE VENKATA JYOTHIRMAI PRATAPA Date: 04.12.2025 MKK HON'BLE DR.
